summary: Instinct bridge, PR 1 (contract and durable records), behind the staged flag instinct_bridge (INSTINCT_BRIDGE_ENABLED in src/shared/bridge.ts, false; SB_INSTINCT_BRIDGE=1 or the backend setting labs.instinct_bridge turns it on; no capability is advertised until the tools ship). src/shared/bridge.ts holds the wire version (1), the seven tool names (search_chats, list_projects, list_recent_chats, start_chat, send_to_chat, read_chat, stop_chat), the three mutating operations, the project policy {project_id, label, machine_id, canonical_local_root, allowed_agents, default_agent, default_model, default_mode, maximum_mode, actions} with defaults auto capped at auto, edit and checks on, commit, push, PR, merge and deploy off, the public project view without the local root, the opaque chat reference {machine_id, chat_id}, the call delivery, chat work, stop and evidence states, the 19 error codes with a structured error and retry advice, the mode check that refuses a mode above the cap instead of changing it, and a canonical input hash for idempotency. An additive migration adds bridge_project_policies (with a revision raised on each save), bridge_calls (unique on operation and idempotency key, with input hash, call id, machine, resolved target, policy revision, state, rejection detail and timestamps; after 90 days a tombstone keeps key, hash and call id, and its key answers request_retired), bridge_origins (one per root chat, resolved through resolveRootThreadId, stamped with the stop generation) and bridge_stop_generation (one monotonic row). src/main/db/bridge.ts reserves calls in an immediate transaction under the call id the relay reserved (or a new one for a local call), moves call states only forward, retires expired calls, recovers calls caught mid-flight at start (recorded becomes rejected with confirmed non-delivery, dispatching becomes delivery_unknown), records and reads origins and reads and advances the stop generation. Settings > Labs gains an Instinct bridge row with a warning that Instinct acts as the owner in allowed projects. Nothing calls these records yet: no relay, no tools and no executable bridge path ship in this part. PR 2 (local read tools): with the flag on, Settings > Labs lists the sidebar projects with a checkbox each (none checked by default); a checked project is saved as a bridge policy under its realpath with the default policy, on this desktop's machine id (the existing hub.installId row), through the admin-scoped bridge:list-projects and bridge:set-project-allowed channels. The Switchboard MCP server gives every local agent list_projects, list_recent_chats, search_chats and read_chat (src/main/bridge/read-service.ts, src/main/mcp/bridge-tools.ts), listed only while the flag is on and refused with bridge_disabled once it is off. The allowlist is applied in SQL before ranking and limits on both the FTS and the fallback message-search path; title matches merge with message hits into one row per root chat (matched_on title, message or both) under the existing word-prefix and archive-word rules; snippets are plain text of at most 240 characters with saved secrets masked; read_chat returns measured status, the latest reply with a partial marker while a turn runs, pending questions and approvals, a bounded masked history window and an opaque since cursor bound to chat, machine and policy revision (unchanged: true or cursor_expired); labels resolve exact id, then exact normalized label, then bounded word-prefix fuzzy, and several plausible matches give ambiguous_target with choices. No answer carries a local path. Results are local only (partial false, no unavailable machines) and evidence is not_measured until the measured-check service. Global search is unchanged. PR 3 (owner delivery): with the flag on the Switchboard MCP server also gives every local agent start_chat, send_to_chat and stop_chat (src/main/bridge/delivery-service.ts), each with an idempotency_key. A call is reserved under (operation, caller-scoped key) with its input hash before any provider action; the same key and body answers from the record (replayed: true), another body gives idempotency_conflict. start_chat resolves an allowed project, refuses a mode above min(policy cap, caller mode) with mode_not_allowed and an agent or model the project does not offer with agent_unavailable and choices, allows one active bridge group per machine (policy_denied while a bridge chat runs or starts), stores the chat, its mode and model and its bridge origin before the provider starts, starts it through startManagedSession and sends the first message through the durable atomic user-turn acceptance with origin bridge-<call id>, so a retry after a crash finds the accepted turn and its message id and sends nothing again. send_to_chat refuses archived chats (chat_archived), open hub children (child_read_only), a chat in a mode wider than the cap and the calling chat itself, resumes a dormant chat through the normal start (else chat_not_resumable), records the bridge origin on the chat and applies peerDelivery: queue by default, steer only when asked, supported and not compacting or stopping, with requested and actual delivery in the answer. stop_chat (allowed from plan mode) fences any start or send of that chat still in flight, takes back the bridge's queued messages only and runs the user's Stop (interrupt, auto-resume disarmed), answering stopping, stopped or stop_unconfirmed. The execution root is realpathed under the policy root before each mutation. A plan-mode caller cannot start or send. No card is shown and the started chat keeps its own approvals and plan mode; nothing goes through the agent peer gate. bridge_calls gains an additive result column (actual delivery, stop status). PR 3 fixes from the packaged test: stop_chat re-sends the Stop until the chat has no turn or start left and answers stopped only then (stop_unconfirmed after 20 s), a steer before the provider's first event and reply queues instead, start_chat saves the resolved account on the chat, and a missing project folder is logged once until it resolves again. Review fixes: agent choices list only agents that can start here (an ACP agent is not offered on a remote backend), a policy default model for another agent is not used, the flag, policy and archive state are re-read before each submit, a dormant chat's folder is checked before its resume, a bridge steer that can no longer land queues at the adapter boundary and the receipt reports the actual queue, the planned delivery is stored before submission for replays, and stop_chat cancels bridge-queued messages every round, covers a delivery_unknown send, is not held up by the owner's held queue, and is stop_unconfirmed when a bridge message cannot be taken back. PR 5 (outbound device enrollment): with the flag on, Settings > Labs enrolls this desktop through the admin-scoped bridge:device-status, bridge:enroll-device, bridge:set-device-label and bridge:remove-device channels. Enroll makes one ECDSA P-256 key pair for machine id hub.installId; the private key is stored in the backend settings row bridge.device (an admin-only settings family) only as the \0SBE sentinel plus the Electron safeStorage ciphertext, as provider instance env is, is never made without a keychain, and a row this build cannot read is never overwritten. The page shows the machine id, the key fingerprint, the status (not enrolled, connecting, connected, retrying or rejected with the relay's code, key unreadable) and the operator command; Remove enrollment deletes the key. While the flag is on and a key exists, the main process keeps one outbound WebSocket to the relay origin (https://bridge.tn07.dev by default; https only, plain http only to 127.0.0.1 or localhost from SB_BRIDGE_RELAY_ORIGIN; TLS validated; User-Agent Switchboard/<version>), signs the relay's challenge over nonce, machine id and relay origin (wire version 1, capability instinct_bridge_v1), sends the allowlisted catalog {project_id, label, default_agent, agents, maximum_mode} with no path after the welcome and after each allowlist change, pings every 30 s and reconnects with backoff. It records the relay's connection generation, refuses a welcome at or below an earlier one and drops frames for another machine or another generation. It runs no command in this part: a command frame is logged with commands_disabled and dropped. scripts/bridge-operator.mjs enrolls, lists and revokes devices with the operator key from Secret Manager switchboard-bridge-operator-key or BRIDGE_OPERATOR_KEY. The relay side (operator endpoints, challenge, fencing, catalogs and list_projects from them) is in tn07-site workers/bridge-relay. PR 6 (stop and recovery controls, high risk) adds src/main/bridge/stop-service.ts, which is not behind the flag so a saved kill, the stop generation, status and stops hold for existing bridge origins. bridge_stop_generation gains killed, kill_pending and the last stop result (additive columns); bridge_origins gains source (local or relay) and stop_state. The relay client takes stop_generation and killed from the welcome and from control frames (validated, invalid ones dropped with invalid_control), and sends stop_ack and kill; command frames stay dropped. A control is recorded before any chat stops, the generation is never lowered, a relay generation with no local result stops every active bridge-origin group (a start in flight, a running or preparing turn including an owner turn the bridge steered into, or bridge-queued messages; bridge-queued messages are taken back and the user's Stop runs), and the ack is confirmed only when every chat stopped. Unrelated chats are never touched. While killed, start_chat and send_to_chat refuse with the new error code killed and confirmed non-delivery; reads and stop_chat work. Settings > Labs has Stop all bridge work (confirm dialog; a new generation, killed, kill sent to the relay now or on the next welcome) and shows the kill, the generation, the last result with unconfirmed chats, active bridge chats, last relay contact and lease expiry, and that a stop also interrupts a steered owner turn. An enrolled desktop clears the kill only through the relay (node scripts/bridge-operator.mjs clear-kill, shown on the page); one that is not enrolled has Allow bridge work again. Nothing clears a kill on its own. A 120 s control lease stops relay-source work when the relay is silent, and a revoked close or a removed enrollment stops it at once; the check runs every 10 s and on powerMonitor resume, which also enforces a saved kill. At start recoverBridgeCalls and retireExpiredBridgeCalls run before the registry (then retire daily), and a stop left pending becomes unconfirmed. Limit auto-resume skips and disarms a bridge chat while killed or when a stop came after its last bridge call. scripts/bridge-operator.mjs adds stop-status, kill, clear-kill and revoke-assistant-key. Both phones decode the new optional SessionSummary.bridgeOrigin {stop} on app:get-projects and label the chat (From the bridge, Bridge stop pending, Bridge stopped, Bridge stop not confirmed); phone management controls are staged behind instinct_bridge_phone_controls for bridge-v2.1. PR 7 (wire the seven tools, high risk: ingress and tool exposure) adds src/main/bridge/command-dispatch.ts. The relay client no longer drops a `command` frame: one for this machine and this connection generation goes to BridgeCommandDispatcher, which checks the frame (wire version 1, a call id, a known tool, object arguments, a whole stop_generation; else invalid_request or unsupported_version, and a frame with no usable call id is dropped), runs the named tool through the SAME typed services the local MCP tools use (read-service.ts for the four reads, delivery-service.ts for start_chat, send_to_chat and stop_chat) and answers with one result frame {type, machine_id, connection_generation, call_id, ok, result | error} on the connection the command arrived on. The relay's result_ack is logged; the work is never run twice, so an ack that never arrives costs nothing and a second frame for a call already running is dropped. A result over 64 KiB is replaced by an internal_error. The error object carries delivered and non_delivery_confirmed: delivered only for delivery_unknown, and non-delivery confirmed for every structured refusal that happens before or instead of a submit. BridgeCaller is now a union: a local agent ({kind: 'local-agent', chatId, mode}) or the owner ({kind: 'owner', callId}). The owner has no calling chat, so no check reads one for it: it never goes through the agent peer gate, is not refused for plan mode, is not blocked as a hub child and gets no chat-scoped key namespace. Its authority is the project policy alone (mode cap, allowed agents, actions); the per-caller mode narrowing applies only to a local agent. recordBridgeOrigin's source is derived from the caller kind (relay for the owner), so the control lease and a revoke stop exactly the owner's work. The owner's idempotency key is relay:<relay call id> and the desktop reserves the call under the relay's call id with its own canonical input digest, before any provider action, so a frame that arrives twice (a relay retry, or after a restart of this desktop) answers from the record and sends nothing again, and the same call id with another body is idempotency_conflict. A start_chat or send_to_chat whose stop_generation is below this desktop's is fenced with policy_denied and confirmed non-delivery; stop_chat is never fenced, because a stop always works. A generation above this desktop's means a control frame was missed, so the stop service's generation-only entry point advanceStopGeneration records it and runs that stop before the new work; a command frame carries no kill state, so that entry point reads the stored kill inside the stop queue and never clears a kill queued behind it. Reads are not fenced. With the flag off every command is refused with bridge_disabled, and the flag, the policy, the realpathed execution root and the kill are read again inside the service right before each mutation, not once at frame arrival. A new error code invalid_request joins the shared list (22 codes). The Labs flag instinct_bridge now advertises the capability instinct_bridge_v1 in the ready frame, which PR 1 deliberately omitted until the tools really ran; the wire version check on the relay socket is unchanged. A chat the relay starts is an ordinary chat: it is a managed root in app:get-projects and carries the bridgeOrigin marker both phones decode (From the bridge, then Bridge stopped after a stop).

desktop.followUpRelease: bridge-v2.1: the release that ships the relay connection, the seven tools and the stop controls (bridge PRs 2 to 8) and keeps instinct_bridge off by default until the owner trial on both computers passes. PR 2 added the allowlist setup in Settings > Labs and the four read tools for local agents; PR 3 adds start_chat, send_to_chat and stop_chat for local agents. PR 5 adds device enrollment and the outbound relay connection (catalog only, no commands). PR 6 adds the stop controls, the control lease and restart and wake enforcement. PR 7 wires the relay's command frames to the seven tools behind the same flag and advertises instinct_bridge_v1.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: bridge-v2.1: phone stop and management controls. PR 6 ships, unflagged because it only reads, the bridge-origin marker on chat rows (SessionSummary.bridgeOrigin {stop}) and its label with the stop state (pending, stopped, not confirmed); an older backend sends no marker and the row is unchanged. Until bridge-v2.1 the owner stops bridge work from desktop Settings > Labs or the operator command. PR 7 changes nothing on the phone: a chat the relay starts arrives through the existing app:get-projects projection with the same bridgeOrigin marker the phones already decode, and no phone code changed.

updateRelease.followUpRelease: bridge-v2.1. PR 1's migration is additive (four new tables) and PR 2 adds no migration and PR 3 adds one nullable column (bridge_calls.result, added only when missing): policies go in the PR 1 table and the machine id reuses the existing hub.installId settings row. The flag stays off by default and advertises no capability. PR 5 adds no migration: the device key is one backend settings row (bridge.device, versioned v1, safeStorage encrypted) and an older build ignores it. The relay deploy needs the BRIDGE_OPERATOR_VERIFIER secret and the BRIDGE_RELAY_ORIGIN var; the Worker entry moved to src/entry.js because workerd refuses an entry module that exports plain values. PR 6 adds only nullable or defaulted columns (bridge_stop_generation.killed, kill_pending, last_result; bridge_origins.source, stop_state), each added only when missing; an older build ignores them. Deferred: the stop supervisor runs inside the app process (a 10 s timer and powerMonitor resume), not as a separate OS process, so after a hard crash the next start reports the stop as unconfirmed instead of watching the process group meanwhile. PR 7 adds no migration and no new stored field: it reserves calls under the relay's call id in the PR 1 ledger and records relay-source origins in the PR 6 column. It does change what a client sees: the ready frame advertises instinct_bridge_v1 while the flag is on, so a relay update still cannot widen project policy and a rollback that turns the flag off refuses every command while the receipts and the stop service stay.

automated: tests/unit/bridge-delivery-service.test.ts (createMigratedDb, the real AtomicUserTurnSubmission and SqliteTurnAcceptanceStore, a fake registry host): start stores the chat, mode and origin before the start and sends one atomic first turn; same key and body replays without a second send, a changed body is idempotency_conflict, another caller's key is separate; mode cap from policy and caller, plan callers refused; agent and model choices; project off the allowlist; bridge_disabled with the flag off on all three; one active bridge group with sends into that chat still accepted; a stop during the start fences it (no turn sent, call rejected with confirmed non-delivery); a crash after the provider took the turn replays the same message id with no second dispatch, a turn left dispatching stays delivery_unknown, a call never dispatched is rejected; idle send is a turn, busy send queues by default, steers when asked, queues while compacting and on an ACP agent; dormant chat resumes through startSession or answers chat_not_resumable; a rotated id reaches the root and submits on the live rotated thread; archived, open child, wider chat mode, moved execution root and the calling chat are refused; a pending approval stays open and read_chat shows it after a send; stop takes back only bridge-queued messages, runs the Stop once, replays as stopped, and a failing Stop is stop_unconfirmed; the MCP tools list seven names and refuse with isError.

PR 3 packaged-test fixes: bridge-delivery-service.test.ts covers a stop right after a start that the provider ignores at first (stopped only after the turn ends, Stop sent more than once), a Stop the provider never takes (stop_unconfirmed), a stop during the start (start refused, nothing sent) and the saved provider account; provider-registry-queued-turns.test.ts checks that the registry blocks a bridge steer until the provider's first event and reply.

tests/unit/bridge-read-service.test.ts (createMigratedDb): the allowlist starts empty, saves the default policy under the realpath and ignores another machine's policy; title-only, message-only and both hits give one row per root chat (a rotated session's hit joins its root); the allowlist applies before the limit on the FTS path and, with messages_fts dropped, on the fallback path; archived chats only with the archive word; an empty index answers empty lists; snippets are plain, at most 240 characters, and mask a saved secret; recent chats order by message time and live activity, not metadata; project and chat labels resolve exactly, fuzzily and as ambiguous_target with choices; a chat outside the allowlist or on another machine is refused; read_chat returns status, latest reply with partial, pending questions and not_measured evidence; the since cursor gives unchanged, then only new messages, and cursor_expired for another chat, a forged cursor and a policy change; no answer holds the project folder path.

tests/unit/secret-request-registry.test.ts (real registry): the four tools are not listed with instinct_bridge off, are listed read-only with it on, and a call after it turns off answers bridge_disabled; bridge:* channels are refused for PHONE_SCOPES and allowed for FULL_SCOPES.
tests/unit/labs-page.test.ts: the project list appears only after the Instinct bridge switch is on, and a checkbox calls setProjectAllowed and shows the saved state.

PR 1 tests (bridge-db, bridge-contract, labs) unchanged and green.
npm run typecheck and npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 pass.

tests/unit/bridge-device-key.test.ts (createMigratedDb, safeStorage fake): the private key round trips only behind the sentinel and ciphertext and signs the hello payload (verified with the public key, P1363 64 bytes); enrolling again keeps the same key; no keychain or an unavailable one refuses and stores nothing; an unreadable, corrupt or plaintext key is key_unreadable and neither key half appears in the log; a row an older run stored is read back and signs (upgrade path); a row of an unknown format is never overwritten until removed.

tests/unit/bridge-relay-client.test.ts: the relay origin accepts https and env-only loopback http and refuses http, ws, paths, queries and user parts; no socket option turns TLS checks off; the client dials wss://<relay>/connect with the Switchboard user agent and signs nonce, machine id and origin; the catalog has only the five public fields even when the source row holds a path; a challenge of another wire version is refused; frames for another machine, an older generation and every command frame are dropped; a welcome at or below an earlier generation is refused; relay refusals are rejected with their code and retried after 30 s, drops after about 1 s; replaced, auth timeout, silence and stop; the link starts only with the flag on and a key, stops when either goes, refuses enrollment while the flag is off or without a keychain, reports an unreadable key and a bad origin; bridgeCatalog holds no path.

tests/unit/labs-page.test.ts: Enroll this Mac calls bridge:enroll-device with the label and shows the machine id, the operator command and the status; tests/unit/settings-device-auth-gate.test.ts pins bridge. as an admin-only settings family.

Live local run (2026-11-06): the real BridgeRelayClient and scripts/bridge-operator.mjs against tn07-site workers/bridge-relay under wrangler dev 4.157.0 (workerd, throwaway keys): assistant key refused on enroll (401) and operator key refused on /mcp (401); an unenrolled device rejected with not_enrolled; enroll, connect, list_projects online from the catalog with no path; a second connection fenced the first (replaced, generation 2); operator list online with no key; revoke closed the socket (revoked), a reconnect stayed revoked and the machine's projects left list_projects; an unauthenticated socket closed after 10 s (4008 auth_timeout); ping answered by the auto-response; no key material in the relay log.

PR 6: tests/unit/bridge-stop-service.test.ts (createMigratedDb, fake host): the control is on disk before any stop starts; generation never lowered and a stale control runs no stop but acks the last result; ack confirmed vs unconfirmed with chat titles; Stop all raises the generation, kills and sends kill; a kill made while disconnected is resent on the next welcome and kept against a relay that moved on, and dropped once the relay echoes it; no automatic clear (stale control, wake, restart); enrolled desktops clear only through the relay, others locally; the lease stops only relay-source work past 120 s or with no contact; revoked and unenrolled stop it at once; wake enforces a saved kill then the lease; start recovers and retires calls and turns a pending stop into unconfirmed; bridgeAutoResumeBlocked after a kill or a later stop.

PR 6: bridge-delivery-service.test.ts: killed refuses start and send with confirmed non-delivery while reads and stop_chat work; a kill during a start fences the turn; stopGroups stops only bridge-origin chats (an unrelated busy chat untouched), takes back bridge-queued messages, stops a steered owner turn and reports one that keeps running as unconfirmed; the relay source filter. limit-resumer.test.ts: a bridge-stopped chat is not resumed and is disarmed. bridge-relay-client.test.ts: welcome stop state passed on or dropped when malformed, control frames for another machine, connection or of the wrong type dropped, nothing before the welcome, stop_ack and kill only when live, last contact, revoked close, commands still dropped. labs-page.test.ts: Stop all only after the confirm, the killed view with the operator command, local clear when not enrolled. Mobile jest home-recents-bridge.test.ts and Android RemoteBridgeOriginDecoderTest decode the marker and labels.

PR 7: tests/unit/bridge-command-dispatch.test.ts (createMigratedDb, the real atomic turn acceptance, the shared fake registry host): the frame shape (no call id, wire version 2, an unknown tool, non-object arguments, a negative stop generation, a missing query or message); every tool refused with the flag off and no provider reached; a full owner call for all seven on an allowed target (start, send, read, recent, search, stop) with no path in any answer; the call recorded under the relay's call id and key relay:<call id>; the owner capped by the project policy alone (full access allowed when the policy allows it, refused when it does not) and still refused on a hub child; a project never allowed and one taken off the allowlist; ambiguous_target with choices on a fuzzy name; a chat whose worktree moved out of the allowed root; an allowed folder that no longer resolves; killed refuses start and send with confirmed non-delivery while read and stop work; a stale stop generation fences start_chat and send_to_chat with confirmed non-delivery but not a read and not stop_chat, which still stops a running chat; a newer one is applied before the work, on a stop too; a repeated start_chat frame and a repeated send_to_chat frame after a rebuilt service send nothing twice; the same call id with another body is idempotency_conflict; the started chat is a managed root in the sidebar projection with the bridgeOrigin marker and the phone labels From the bridge and Bridge stopped. bridge-stop-service.test.ts: advanceStopGeneration records a newer generation, runs that stop and acks it with the stored kill untouched, and never clears a kill queued ahead of it on the stop queue, while a relay control at the current generation still clears one.

PR 7: tests/unit/bridge-relay-client.test.ts adds command frames: one command runs once and answers with one result frame on the same connection; a refusal goes back as ok: false with the error; a frame for another machine, an older generation or a call already running never runs; an answer that resolves after a reconnect is dropped (stale_connection) instead of being sent on the new connection; a result the relay never acks is not resent and the work is not run again, and a result_ack with stored: false is logged.
